verses.text: Around that time, King Herod began attacking some people in the church.
He had James, John’s brother, killed with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jewish leaders, he arrested Peter too. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
Herod put Peter in prison and assigned four squads of four soldiers to guard him. He planned to bring him out for the people after Passover.
So Peter was locked up, while the church kept praying earnestly to God for him. 🙏
That night, just before Herod planned to bring him out, Peter was asleep between two soldiers, chained on both sides. Guards were stationed at the prison entrance.
Suddenly, an angel of the Lord stood there, and light filled the cell. The angel nudged Peter awake and said, “Get up—quick!” The chains fell off Peter’s hands.
The angel told him, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did. Then the angel said, “Put on your coat and follow me.”
Peter followed him out, but he had no idea it was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.
They passed the first guard, then the second, and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened by itself. They went outside, walked down one street, and then the angel suddenly left him.
Then Peter came to his senses. “Now I know for sure: the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod—and from everything the Jewish people expected to happen to me.”
Once he realized that, he went to Mary’s house. She was John, also called Mark’s, mother. Many believers were gathered there, praying.
When Peter knocked at the outer gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
She recognized Peter’s voice and got so excited she forgot to open the gate. She ran inside and announced, “Peter’s standing outside!”
They told her, “You’re out of your mind!” But she kept insisting it was true. “Then it must be his angel,” they said.
Meanwhile Peter kept knocking. When they opened the gate and saw him, they were stunned.
He motioned with his hand for them to be quiet, then told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other believers,” he said. Then he left and went somewhere else.
When morning came, the soldiers were in total confusion over what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched for him but couldn’t find him. He questioned the guards and ordered them executed. Then he left Judea for Caesarea and stayed there.
Herod was furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came together to seek peace. First, they won over Blastus, the king’s personal aide. They needed the king’s region to supply their food.
On the appointed day, Herod dressed in royal robes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to them.
The crowd shouted, “That’s a god speaking, not a human!”
At once, an angel of the Lord struck Herod because he took the glory that belonged to God. Worms ate him, and he died.
But God’s message kept spreading and gaining ground. 🌱
After completing their service in Jerusalem, Barnabas and Saul returned to Antioch, bringing John, also called Mark, with them.
